members.text: Accelerating trunk rotation all the way through to the target instead of decelerating short of the target to release the shoulder
The player fails to freeze or decelerate the trunk right before contact, leaking rotational momentum instead of transferring it into the arm.
Trunk spins continuously without an anchor to decelerate, preventing momentum transfer to the arm and racket.

groups.why_run1: Failing to decelerate the rotating trunk before contact prevents rotational momentum from transferring into the arm and racket.
groups.why_run2: Failing to decelerate or brake trunk rotation before contact, preventing momentum transfer into the arm and racket.

members.text: Pulling too close to the body or relying excessively on rotational body mechanics rather than pulling well out in front.
Catching the ball too late with the pull slot set too close to the stomach rather than out in front.

groups.why_run1: Pulling or making contact too close to the body or stomach instead of out in front.
groups.why_run2: Setting the pull slot or pulling too close to the body rather than well out in front.

members.text: Letting go of the racket with the non-dominant hand too early instead of supporting it deep into the forward swing.
Initiating the stroke solely with one hand instead of executing a two-handed forward movement into the pull slot.

groups.why_run1: Failing to use both hands together into the forward swing, letting go or using one hand too early.
groups.why_run2: Releasing the non-dominant hand too early instead of using both hands to guide the racket forward into the pull slot.

members.text: The player lets the hips drift forward and slides the knee forward over the toes instead of hinging at the hips and keeping the hips behind.
Hips extending forward in front of the shoulders with knees forward and chest up (quad dominant posture) rather than maintaining a hip hinge.

groups.why_run1: Allowing the hips and knees to slide or extend forward instead of maintaining a hip hinge.
groups.why_run2: Allowing the hips and knees to thrust forward instead of maintaining a hip hinge.

members.text: Releasing the racket directly towards the ball instead of directing the first vector outward prevents the shoulder from adducting through contact to create velocity.
Directing the elbow or racket straight towards the ball rather than driving out in the direction the chest is facing.

groups.why_run1: Directing the arm or racket straight toward the ball rather than driving outward away from the body.
groups.why_run2: Directing the racket or elbow straight toward the ball rather than driving outward along the chest vector.

members.text: The player's brain misinterprets the fast rolling speed during the follow-through as the primary hitting acceleration zone.
Confusing the rolling follow-through / windshield wiper action with the back-to-front flip and hit release.

groups.why_run1: Confusing or misinterpreting the rolling follow-through with the primary forward acceleration and release into the ball.
groups.why_run2: Mistaking the rolling follow-through or windshield-wiper action for the primary forward acceleration and release phase.

members.text: Players post-process their own shot and critique technique rather than locking into the opponent.
Mental evaluation and technical focus on the serve leak into the rally, preventing immediate transition into receiving mode.

groups.why_run1: Evaluating and critiquing stroke mechanics after hitting instead of immediately engaging in the ongoing rally.
groups.why_run2: Mentally evaluating technique from the previous shot instead of shifting focus forward to the opponent and the incoming rally.

members.text: Anxiety spikes to maximum levels rather than staying at an optimal midpoint (such as 7 or 8 out of 10), triggering maladaptive physical reactions.
Players fail to calibrate anxiety properly, either over-hyping and blasting neutral balls or lacking alertness to attack short balls.

groups.why_run1: Failing to regulate anxiety at an optimal level, leading to maladaptive over-arousal and poor execution.
groups.why_run2: Failing to calibrate anxiety to an optimal level, resulting in maladaptive physical responses and poor shot execution.

members.text: Conceiving the serve internally as a down-to-up or low-to-high vertical motion prevents the body from loading in the horizontal in-to-out plane.
The player attempts to throw the racket up or down-and-up directly at the ball rather than throwing it out to the hitting side.
also_worded: Players attempt to use a flat serve throwing trajectory or actively throw straight forward at the service box where they are aiming.

groups.why_run1: Directing or conceiving the swing as a vertical upward path toward the ball instead of throwing the racket outward along an in-to-out path.
groups.why_run2: Swinging vertically up toward the ball instead of directing the racket outward in an in-to-out path.

members.text: Spacing too close to the body, which requires a linear push and inhibits shoulder external/internal rotation
Swinging too close to the body crowds the contact point and prevents the hand from naturally tugging back on the handle to whip the racket.

groups.why_run1: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)
groups.why_run2: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)

members.text: Collapsing elbow space and relaxing the upper back removes the structural leverage required for the pecs and arm to press forward.
The elbow drops in toward the body because the back, rotator cuff, scapula, and chest fail to stabilize it up in a throwing posture.

groups.why_run1: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)
groups.why_run2: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)

members.text: The player steps forward with the foot but leaves their body weight and head behind rather than transferring them over the front hip.
Failing to transfer weight cleanly onto the front foot anchor at finish.

groups.why_run1: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)
groups.why_run2: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)

members.text: The torso rotates on a flat horizontal plane parallel to the court instead of tilting on an upward slant with the off-shoulder rising.
Keeping shoulders level on low balls prevents spinal side bend, causing core tension to collapse and forcing the elbow to drop into an arm-dominant swing.
The player lacks spine side bending on the way forward into contact.

groups.why_run1: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)
groups.why_run2: confirmed by mech_merge_from_review (CC same_mechanism + 2 Gemini yes)
